title: add jsonschema strict-mode error reporting and openai compatibility for response_format
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Improve developer experience and reliability for response_format=json_schema use. This PR adds strict-mode validation error reporting, aligns behavior with OpenAI compatibility expectations, and improves migration paths for existing callers. Summary of changes: - Introduce response_format.strict boolean that enforces exact schema conformance. When strict=true, the runtime validates responses against the provided JSON Schema and returns structured validation errors with stable error codes and guidance for common fix paths. - Add OpenAI-compatible error mapping: validation errors are surfaced under the same top-level error shapes used by the OpenAI compatibility layer so SDKs can handle them uniformly. - Implement a graceful fallback policy where servers can (configurable) attempt to auto-correct common issues (e.g., missing optional fields that have defaults, numeric-as-string coercion) and surface those corrections in a warnings array when strict=false. - Improve per-request telemetry: validation_result fields are emitted to tracing/span metadata and the per-route dashboard; includes validation error codes and short hashes for deduping. - Update API docs and SDK stubs to include response_format examples and recommended error handling patterns. Implementation notes: - Server-side: added a new JsonSchemaValidator component used by the response_format pipeline. Validation is schema-first and uses a deterministic traversal to generate stable error codes. - OpenAI compat: we added a compat translation layer that maps our validation_result -> openai_error format and preserves model output text for debugging. - Tests: unit tests for validator edge cases, e2e tests covering strict=true/false, auto-correct flows, and SDK compatibility tests. - Docs: included examples for strict mode, non-strict mode with auto-corrections, and migration guidance. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains strict=false and unchanged for existing calls. When consumers opt into strict=true, they will get structured validation errors and a non-zero HTTP 422 for schema violations. Migration path is documented and SDK behavior updated to provide helpers that call the fallback-correct endpoints. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag for the OpenAI-compat API surface for 2 weeks in canary, then gradual percentage rollout with telemetry monitoring enabled. See linked Linear tickets for rollout gating. Checklist: - [x] Validator implementation - [x] OpenAI compat mapping - [x] Telemetry and tracing hooks - [x] SDK updates and tests - [x] Docs examples and migration guide
